## PR Description

Closes #1406
### What changed
Added the configurable specialist-reviewer pool (gh-1406): a shared base contract for every PR-review leg plus repo-tunable specialist reviewers (a `security` reviewer ships first), resolved by `js/common/reviewPool.js` and enforced at merge time — a PR never merges while a required reviewer lacks a same-head PASS marker on the current head.

### Key decisions
- Reviewers are data, not code: factory `instructions/review/*.json` define them; repo `.dmtools/review/*.json` may only TUNE factory reviewers (`isEnabled`, `rounds`, `triggerPaths`, `options`, `model`) — re-defining contract fields is a hard error, and duplicate reviewer names (previously a silent merge) now fail the pool load.
- One marker grammar (`js/common/reviewPoolMarkers.js`) rides `reviewVerdicts.parseMarkerComments` with machineAuthor attribution; tuning-merge (`reviewPoolMerge.js`) stays a CRAP-split module out of the loader.
- The merge gate reads comments once per run; the pool clause runs as phase 0 before the thread census. A broken comment read fails CLOSED there (it must not classify as "no markers" — #1319 parity); the verdict gate's fail-open absorb is unchanged (gh-1416).
- §8 CI gate: `scripts/validate-review-skills.js` (wired into `quality.yml`) validates lenses, duplicate names, same-name tuning and prompt targets; `instructions/pr_review/base/` carries the shared leg contract — including `review_verdict_rules.md`, moved into `base/` per the ticket §1 layout, with the #605 pack-reachability anchor following it.
- `reviewPolicy` gains `reviewers` + `promptAppend` (strictness preserved); `pr_test_automation_review` migrates onto the same base set; the base role line drops "& Security Expert".

### How to verify
```bash
DEFAULT_TRACKER=jira dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # full unit suite — env pin mirrors the CI harness (node run shims java getenv to null); the dmtools host leaks the deployment's DEFAULT_TRACKER into tracker-default tests
node scripts/validate-review-skills.js .                      # §8 gate — 2 factory reviewers, 0 errors
```

But anonymous inline functions/callbacks (arrow functions passed to `.map()`, `.filter()`) DO count toward the enclosing function unless extracted.

The `validateSkillDefinition` CC 29 — manual count gives ~15ish; the difference could be from logical operators (`||`, `&&`) which each add 1.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `instructionOverrides.<contextId>` — replace `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent
- `agentParamPatches.<contextId>` — patch `agentParams` fields for a specific agent
- `globalCliPrompts` — prompt files appended to **every** agent's CLI input (inject-to-all)
- `globalAdditionalInstructions` — instruction files appended to **every** agent's `agentParams.instructions`

**Example — inject codegraph into all agents without repeating per context:**
```js
// .dmtools/config.js
module.exports = {
    globalCliPrompts: [
        './agents/instructions/common/codegraph_tools.md'
    ],
    cliPrompts: {
        story_development: ['./.dmtools/prompts/development_focus.md'],
        pr_review:         ['./.dmtools/prompts/review_focus.md']
        // codegraph_tools.md is injected automatically into all agents above
    }
};
```

Global entries are merged **after** per-agent entries so they always appear last.

### SM rules override and custom agents
`js/smAgent.js` supports full and partial SM customization from `.dmtools/config.js`.

**Precedence**
- Base rules come from `sm.json` (`jobParams.rules`)
- If `config.smRules` is set, it **fully replaces** base rules
- If `config.smRuleOverrides` is set, it patches rules by `configFile`

**Common use cases**
- Disable most default rules and keep only one:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRuleOverrides: {
    "agents/story_questions.json": { enabled: true },
    "agents/story_development.json": { enabled: false },
    "agents/pr_review.json": { enabled: false }
  }
};
```

- Full replacement with custom agents:
```js
module.exports = {
  smRules: [
    {
      description: "Run only custom intake flow",
      jql: "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype = Story AND status = 'To Do'",
      configFile: "agents/my_custom_intake.json",
      skipIfLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      addLabel: "sm_my_custom_intake_triggered",
      enabled: true
    }
  ]
};
```

**Rule fields supported by SM**
- `description`, `jql`, `configFile` (required for practical execution)
- `enabled` (set `false` to disable)
- `skipIfLabel` / `skipIfLabels`, `addLabel`
- `targetStatus`, `limit`, `localExecution`
- `configPath` (per-rule project config override for multi-project orchestration)

### Figma design lookup
Any agent that writes or reviews requirements-facing content (questions, descriptions, acceptance criteria, solution/design analysis, dev/test scoping) must treat the linked Figma design as a primary source, not an optional nice-to-have — a story/question/AC that ignores an available design is incomplete, the same way ignoring the code would be.

- **If a ticket/story already links a specific Figma file or node** (a `/file/` or `/design/` URL, optionally with `node-id`): open it directly with `figma_get_file_structure` / `figma_get_layers` / `figma_download_image_of_file` (see `instructions/common/media_handling.md`) before writing output.
- **If only a team- or project-level Figma URL is known** (e.g. a `.../team/<teamId>/...` "files" listing link, typically stored as project config rather than on the ticket itself): resolve it top-down with `figma_list_team_projects` → `figma_list_project_files` to find the file matching the current feature/epic, then drill into it as above. Match by file name against the feature/epic name; if no file name matches, say so explicitly rather than silently skipping the design check.
- **If the design is genuinely unavailable** (no link resolves, access error, no matching file after searching): say so explicitly in the output instead of proceeding as if no design existed — this is the same "unavailable artifact" handling already required by `instructions/common/acceptance_criteria_quality.md`.
- Never fabricate UI/UX details (copy, layout, states) that should come from Figma — pull them from the design or ask a question, don't guess.
- This is process guidance, not a project config — the actual team/project URLs and file-naming convention for a given product live in that product's `.dmtools/instructions/goal/goal.md` or `.dmtools/config.js`, never here.

### Output JSON discipline
When agents produce JSON output files, keep them compact (status, IDs, paths, short summaries). Put large text in separate `.md` files and reference them by path.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

7:#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
8:#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
9:#   asset        crap-baseline.json
13:#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
16:#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
26:#   ratchet step re-runs crap4js with --require-coverage over production js/**.
29:# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
33:# `crap4js duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci`; a
53:# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
54:# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
73:  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
74:  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels
82:  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
84:  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
86:  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
87:  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'
120:  crap:
213:        # a raw copy has no coverage, so every function in it would drop out
215:        # verbatim below): the harness itself (js/unit-tests/testRunner.js —
216:        # it redeclares its shared loaders by design) and js/test/**
217:        # (node:test suites run outside the harness).
220:            --exclude 'js/unit-tests/testRunner.js' --exclude 'js/test/**' \
234:      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
235:        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
237:        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
241:          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
242:          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
243:            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
244:            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Runtime-artifact guard (tracked artifacts / tracked-but-ignored)
        # gh-1365: pipeline-owned runtime artifacts must never be tracked — a modified
        # TRACKED artifact in a runner workspace blocks every dev-leg checkout (the
        # gh-1358/.dmtools-target-workingdir incident), while an untracked+ignored
        # copy is harmless by construction. Both checks are read-only `git ls-files`
        # queries evaluated against the checked-out INDEX — no working-dir state is
        # consulted, so dirty runner workspaces cannot influence the verdict:
        #  1. tracked files matching ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt — the checked-in
        #     gitignore-style list deployments extend WITHOUT touching this workflow;
        #  2. tracked files matching the repo's own ignore rules (`--exclude-standard`)
        #     — the "tracked but ignored" state, i.e. the missed-cleanup signature.
        # Any hit fails the job naming the file and the exact remediation (never just
        # a count); both checks always run so one bad tree reports every violation.
        run: |
          set -e
          patterns="ci/runtime-artifact-patterns.txt"
          status=0
          report="$(mktemp)"

          hits="$(git ls-files --ignored --cached --exclude-from="$patterns")"
          if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
            status=1
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked runtime artifacts (FAIL)"
              echo
              echo "Tracked files match \`$patterns\` — runtime artifacts must never be tracked. Untrack each one:"
              echo
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                echo "- \`$f\` — run \`git rm --cached \"$f\"\` and add the path to .gitignore"
                echo "::error file=$f::tracked runtime artifact matches $patterns — untrack it: git rm --cached \"$f\" and add the path to .gitignore"
              done <<EOF
          $hits
          EOF
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          else
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked runtime artifacts (pass)"
              echo
              echo "No tracked file matches \`$patterns\`."
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          fi

          ignored="$(git ls-files --ignored --cached --exclude-standard)"
          if [ -n "$ignored" ]; then
            status=1
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked-but-ignored files (FAIL)"
              echo
              echo "These tracked files match the repo's own .gitignore rules but are still tracked (the missed-cleanup signature — untrack so the ignore rule takes effect):"
              echo
              while IFS= read -r f; do
                echo "- \`$f\` — run \`git rm --cached \"$f\"\`"
                echo "::error file=$f::tracked but matches .gitignore — untrack it: git rm --cached \"$f\""
              done <<EOF
          $ignored
          EOF
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          else
            {
              echo "## Runtime-artifact guard: tracked-but-ignored files (pass)"
              echo
              echo "No tracked-but-ignored files."
              echo
            } >> "$report"
          fi

          cat "$report"
          cat "$report" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          exit $status

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        id: instrument
        # --exit-on-error: a file that fails to instrument (e.g. a duplicate
        # top-level declaration) FAILS the job instead of being copied raw —
        # a raw copy has no coverage, so every function in it would drop out
        # of the CRAP gate unnoticed. Intentionally uninstrumented (copied
        # verbatim below): the harness itself (js/unit-tests/testRunner.js —
        # it redeclares its shared loaders by design) and js/test/**
        # (node:test suites run outside the harness).
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --exit-on-error \
            --exclude 'js/unit-tests/testRunner.js' --exclude 'js/test/**' \
            --cwd . . "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only instrumented sources — add the
          # json/md/sh/.mjs/.cjs payloads the suite reads (configs,
          # instructions, prompts, fixtures; .mjs/.cjs stay raw as before)…
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # …and the intentionally uninstrumented .js files excluded above.
          rsync -a --ignore-existing --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)

- name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          # Production functions without a CRAP score (N/A coverage or a parse
          # failure) are invisible to the ratchet above — fail on any of them.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" js \
            --exclude 'js/unit-tests/**' --exclude 'js/test/**' --exclude 'js/integration-tests/**' \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 \
            --require-coverage > /dev/null || code=2
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Review skill files (gh-1406 §8 — lens/contract CI gate)
        # The reviewer pool's skill files are CONTRACT, not prose: every
        # reviewer (factory instructions/review/*.json + repo .dmtools/review/*.json)
        # must resolve to an existing non-empty lens, same-name files may only
        # TUNE factory reviewers, duplicate names are rejected, and the
        # promptAppend / reviewPolicy.reviewers targets must exist. Fails the
        # PR before a misconfigured reviewer silently drops out of the pool.
        if: always() && steps.instrument.outcome != 'skipped'
        run: node scripts/validate-review-skills.js .

      - name: Module-size ratchet (<= 800 lines / 40 top-level functions per module)
        # Per-function CRAP never flags a god module made of small functions.
        # Production modules (js/**, tests excluded) must stay within 800
        # physical lines and 40 top-level functions; modules already over a
        # limit are pinned in ci/module-size-baseline.json with their current
        # size and may only shrink (crap4js module-size --baseline). After
        # splitting a pinned module, lower its pin (re-run with
        # --write-baseline) so the gain is locked in.
        if: always() && steps.instrument.outcome != 'skipped'
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" module-size \
            --exclude 'js/unit-tests/**' --exclude 'js/test/**' --exclude 'js/integration-tests/**' \
            --baseline ci/module-size-baseline.json js

      - name: Nesting gate (control-flow nesting <= 5)
        # Pre-existing offenders carry a `// ignore:nesting` marker above the
        # function; new deep nesting fails.
        if: always() && steps.instrument.outcome != 'skipped'
        run: '"$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" nesting js'

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e

# Review Policy

Preset: `default` — resolved from: projectConfig.reviewPolicy (resolution chain: projectConfig.reviewPolicy → workflow jobParams → built-in default).
Verification: `filter` — rework/polish-tier findings are re-verified by a fresh-context filter pass before posting (keep | demote | drop); drops become digest lines, demotes tier downgrades.
Every verdict on this PR is traceable to this table.

| Severity | Round | Fix | Gates approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | rework | mandatory | YES |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | rework | mandatory | YES |
| 💡 SUGGESTION | polish | mandatory | no |
| 🪶 NIT | none | opportunistic | no |

Verification: `filter` — rework/polish-tier findings are re-verified by a fresh-context filter pass before posting (keep | demote | drop); drops become digest lines, demotes tier downgrades.

Bounds: polishMaxThreads=6 · polishMaxChangedLines=80 · opportunisticMaxThreads=8 · opportunisticSameFilesOnly=true · densityMin=2 · densityMax=8 · sweepBatch=10 · sweepMaxAgeDays=30

Density cap (💡/🪶 threads only; 🚨/⚠️ never capped): allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8).
Rank your findings and post the top-K as threads; the overflow becomes a ranked digest list in the general comment. The census counts posted threads + digest lines.

Machine enforcement: the approval is recomputed from the severity census + this policy — the model verdict is advisory. Any 🚨 or ⚠️ open → REQUEST_CHANGES; only 💡/🪶 → APPROVE.
## Downgrade protocol

A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification** in the census (the thread reply and the response summary: why this is not maintainability debt). A silent downgrade does not exist: the next review round re-raises it as ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. A justified downgrade lets a false-⚠️ review converge to APPROVE without a code change.# Pull Request Information

## PR Description

Closes #1406
### What changed
Added the configurable specialist-reviewer pool (gh-1406): a shared base contract for every PR-review leg plus repo-tunable specialist reviewers (a `security` reviewer ships first), resolved by `js/common/reviewPool.js` and enforced at merge time — a PR never merges while a required reviewer lacks a same-head PASS marker on the current head.

### Key decisions
- Reviewers are data, not code: factory `instructions/review/*.json` define them; repo `.dmtools/review/*.json` may only TUNE factory reviewers (`isEnabled`, `rounds`, `triggerPaths`, `options`, `model`) — re-defining contract fields is a hard error, and duplicate reviewer names (previously a silent merge) now fail the pool load.
- One marker grammar (`js/common/reviewPoolMarkers.js`) rides `reviewVerdicts.parseMarkerComments` with machineAuthor attribution; tuning-merge (`reviewPoolMerge.js`) stays a CRAP-split module out of the loader.
- The merge gate reads comments once per run; the pool clause runs as phase 0 before the thread census. A broken comment read fails CLOSED there (it must not classify as "no markers" — #1319 parity); the verdict gate's fail-open absorb is unchanged (gh-1416).
- §8 CI gate: `scripts/validate-review-skills.js` (wired into `quality.yml`) validates lenses, duplicate names, same-name tuning and prompt targets; `instructions/pr_review/base/` carries the shared leg contract — including `review_verdict_rules.md`, moved into `base/` per the ticket §1 layout, with the #605 pack-reachability anchor following it.
- `reviewPolicy` gains `reviewers` + `promptAppend` (strictness preserved); `pr_test_automation_review` migrates onto the same base set; the base role line drops "& Security Expert".

if: always() && steps.instrument.outcome != 'skipped'
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" module-size \
            --exclude 'js/unit-tests/**' --exclude 'js/test/**' --exclude 'js/integration-tests/**' \
            --baseline ci/module-size-baseline.json js

      - name: Nesting gate (control-flow nesting <= 5)
        # Pre-existing offenders carry a `// ignore:nesting` marker above the
        # function; new deep nesting fails.
        if: always() && steps.instrument.outcome != 'skipped'
        run: '"$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" nesting js'

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          node ci/duplicationRatchet.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" duplication-baseline.json "$code"

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then

# gh-1406 rework — quality-gate (CRAP ratchet) fix

## Issues/Notes

- **Open review threads: 0.** `pr_discussions_raw.json` carries no open threads (`"threads": []`), so `outputs/review_replies.json` is written as `{ "replies": [] }` — nothing to answer, no thread state changed.
- **Merge conflicts: none** (no `merge_conflicts.md` in the input; `git diff --check` is clean).
- **CI failures on `6253aa87` (PR #1465): the `crap` job, both occurrences, same root cause** — `CRAP ratchet failed: CRAP may only decrease.` The suite itself was green (10721 passed); every other gate in the job passed at CI time (validate-review-skills ✅, module-size ✅ "243 modules within 800 lines / 40 top-level functions", nesting ✅ "17531 methods within nesting 5", duplication ratchet ✅). `ci_violations.json` counts `owned: 0` (no attributable `path:line` rows — the 20 "unknown" entries are log noise from the repo's own gate tests), but the ratchet verdict names the failing functions explicitly, and all of them live in files this PR creates/touches — so they are owned here. **Owned set: 22 NEW > 8 functions.** No foreign/infra reds.
- **Root cause:** `CRAP = CC²·(1−cov)¹⁰⁰ + CC ≥ CC`, so any function with cyclomatic complexity > 8 can never pass the threshold-8 ratchet regardless of coverage; functions at CC ≤ 8 need ordinary coverage (several new helpers also had **0% coverage**, e.g. `poolSummaryLine` CRAP 72 at cov 0%). The fix is structural: split every over-threshold function so each piece is CC ≤ 8 and covered.

## Owned CI violations — every item `fixed`

| Function (CI-reported CRAP) | File | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|
| `buildPoolPacket` 22 | js/common/reviewPoolMerge.js | split → `poolCensusLineOf` 5.0, `highWeightPacketLineOf` 5.0, `droppedPoolPacketLineOf`, `droppedPoolLocOf` 5.0, `pushMappedLines`; parent now 6.0 |
| `validateSkillDefinition` 33.6 | js/common/reviewPool.js | validation moved to the new `js/common/reviewPoolSchema.js` and split (`skillIdentityOf`, `defaulted*`, `skillUnknownFieldWarnings`, …); entry point now CC 2, CRAP 2.0 |
| `resolvePool` 22.2 | js/common/reviewPool.js | split into `loadFactoryDirs` / `loadRepoDir` / `applyPolicyTuning` / `appendFileReadable` / `resolveAppendPaths`; parent now 5.0 |
| `validateRepoTuning` 16.1 | js/common/reviewPool.js | schema-layer split (`repoTuningOf`, `repoTuningFieldOf`, `repoTunedModelOf`); now 5.0 |
| `buildPoolOutcomeMarkerComment` 15 | js/common/reviewPoolMarkers.js | split → `poolOutcomeEntriesOf` / `poolOutcomeNamesOf` |
| `validateReviewerTuning` 14.1 | js/common/reviewPolicy.js | trio delegated to `reviewPoolSchema.js` (`reviewerTunedModelOf` / `reviewerTunedOptionsOf` / `reviewerTunedFieldOf`); now 5.0 |
| `loadRepoDir` 13.7 | js/common/reviewPool.js | split into `loadRepoEntry` / `tuneFactoryEntry` / `defineRepoEntry` |
| `stampRequiredReviewerHold` 12.6 | js/common/mergeGate.js | split → `requiredReviewerEscalates`, `requiredHoldDedupOf`, `postRequiredReviewerHoldMarker`; parent now 3.0 |
| `readJson` 12.9 | js/common/reviewPool.js | split → `readTextSoft` / `isEmptyText`; now 4.0 |
| `mergeCandidateLists` 10 | js/common/reviewPoolMerge.js | split → `mergeOneCandidate`; parent now 6.0 |
| `poolPhase` 10 | js/common/mergeGate.js | split → `poolCommentListOf` (+ the unreachable `!out.head` branch removed — `sameHead`'s falsy guard already routes a missing head to fail-open); now 5.0 |
| `roundsDecide` 10 | js/common/reviewPool.js | split into per-concern helpers; now 5.0 |
| `applyWeightedRetention` 11 | js/common/reviewPoolMerge.js | split → `highWeightRefusalOf` 6.0, `weightedRefusalNoteOf`; parent now 5.0 |
| `highWeightOutcomesOf` 9.4 | js/common/reviewPoolMerge.js | split → `highWeightOutcomeRowOf` 6.0; parent now 5.0 |
| `droppedPoolCandidateLine` 9.4 | js/common/reviewPoolMerge.js | split → `poolCandidateLocOf` 4.0, `poolCandidateClaimOf` 3.0; parent now 4.0 |
| `poolRecordFromPayload` 9.1 | js/common/reviewPoolMarkers.js | split → `poolEntryListOf` |
| `buildRequiredReviewerHoldMarker` 9 | js/common/reviewPoolMarkers.js | split → `requiredHoldPayload` / `requiredHoldNote` |
| `validateReviewersTuning` 8.3 | js/common/reviewPolicy.js | delegated to `reviewPoolSchema.js`; now 6.0 |
| `validatePromptAppend` 8.3 | js/common/reviewPolicy.js | delegated to `reviewPoolSchema.js` (`promptAppendKeyOf`); now 6.0 |
| `entryNameOf` 8.3 | js/common/reviewPool.js | split → `hasJsonSuffix` / `jsonFileNamesOf` / `repoEntryNameOf`; now 6.0 |
| `listJsonFiles` 8.2 | js/common/reviewPool.js | split → `jsonFileNamesOf`; now 5.0 |
| `poolSummaryLine` 72 (CC 8 @ **0% coverage**) | js/common/reviewPool.js | covered by new unit tests; now CC 8 @ 100% → CRAP 8.0 |

Measured after the fix (local CI-parity run, same pinned tools `IstiN/crap4js#2d99360` + `nyc@17`, released `crap-baseline.json`): **`0 regression(s), 0 new over threshold` — ratchet exit 0**; every function above now measures ≤ 8.0 at 100% (or 90.9%) coverage. All 22 items: `fixed`.

## Approach

1. **TDD on the gate itself (RED):** reproduced the CI failure locally with the exact CI pipeline — `nyc instrument` the tree (same excludes), run the full suite under coverage via `ci/run_with_coverage.js`, then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline crap-baseline.json`. First local run: exit 2 with `4 NEW > 8` remaining (the earlier legs of this lap had already taken CI's 22 down to 4 via the `reviewPoolSchema.js`/`reviewPool.js`/`mergeGate.js` splits).
2. **GREEN, surgically:** split only the four still-over-threshold functions in `js/common/reviewPoolMerge.js` (`applyWeightedRetention`, `highWeightOutcomesOf`, `droppedPoolCandidateLine`, `buildPoolPacket`) into single-purpose helpers, each CC ≤ 6, preserving exact behavior (100%-covered existing tests acted as the behavior guard; the split helpers all measure 100% covered). No untouched/already-approved PR code was rewritten — the lap's diff is confined to the six pool/gate modules named above plus their unit tests.
3. **Full verification on the frozen tree** (see Test Coverage) before committing; `dart_format` is not applicable (JS-only PR, no Dart in the diff).

## Files Modified

This lap (final leg) — `js/common/reviewPoolMerge.js` only:
- `applyWeightedRetention` → `highWeightRefusalOf` + `weightedRefusalNoteOf` (+ doc consolidation)
- `highWeightOutcomesOf` → `highWeightOutcomeRowOf`
- `droppedPoolCandidateLine` → `poolCandidateLocOf` + `poolCandidateClaimOf`
- `buildPoolPacket` → `poolCensusLineOf` + `highWeightPacketLineOf` + `droppedPoolPacketLineOf` + `droppedPoolLocOf` + `pushMappedLines`

Earlier legs of the same rework lap (already on the branch, same owned set):
- `js/common/reviewPoolSchema.js` (new) — policy/skill validation extracted from `reviewPolicy.js` + `reviewPool.js`
- `js/common/reviewPool.js` — IO/pool layer split (loaders, readers, resolvePool, roundsDecide, poolSummaryLine tests)
- `js/common/reviewPolicy.js` — trio delegation to the schema module
- `js/common/mergeGate.js` — `poolPhase` / `stampRequiredReviewerHold` splits
- `js/common/reviewPoolMarkers.js` — marker builder splits
- `js/unit-tests/test_reviewPool*.js`, `test_reviewPolicy.js`, `test_mergeGate.js`, `test_retryMergeGithubPR.js`, `node_testRunner.js`, `testRunner.js` — regression tests for the split surface (10760 tests total, up from 10721 at CI time)

## Test Coverage

🚨 **BLOCKING: CI red — CRAP ratchet fails on `walk` (quality job exit 2)**

The `crap` check fails on head `980ac31a` (ci_failures.md):

```
NEW > 8  js/unit-tests/test_instructionRefs.js::walk: 15
0 regression(s), 1 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed

```

The new `v1ShimIndex()` helper (test_instructionRefs.js:200) inlines one `walk` closure carrying all of the branch work: the `file_list` shape normalization, dotfile skip, the `file_exists` dual-shape dir test (`ex === true || (ex && typeof ex === 'object' && ex.exists === true)`), the `.md`/dir fork, the banner cut ternary, the missing-banner `continue`, and the `livePat` exec loop — CC lands the function over the CRAP 8 threshold at its measured coverage.

Fix per the repo's CRAP-split convention: extract small pure helpers — e.g. `isDirEntry(ex)`, `shimBannerPaths(txt)` (returns the live paths named by a banner), and a per-entry step — and pin each with direct unit tests, or extend R13's fixtures so `walk`'s branches run under the coverage harness. Either way the ratchet must go green; everything else in this PR is already green (unit suite 10807 passed, 0 failed).

### 2. `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs628xSH` — **unknown** (`scripts/validate-review-skills.js:152`)

⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: validator resolves skill-file `lens` paths against the wrong root — false-fails on the documented consuming-repo layout**

`scripts/validate-review-skills.js` resolves **every** path through `toRepoRelative` (`path.join(repoRoot, p)`, lines 112–131), but the factory skill files' `lens` field carries a **pack-relative** path (`"instructions/pr_review/generalist/lens.md"`). In this checkout the two roots coincide, so the CI step passes — but the script's own documented usage is the consuming repo ("from the consuming repo root, with the agents pack available", header; `factoryDirs` even defaults to `agents/instructions/review`, line 90). With the pack at `agents/`, `readFile` looks for `<repoRoot>/instructions/pr_review/generalist/lens.md` while the file lives at `<repoRoot>/agents/instructions/...` — the read misses, and the check-3 split (lines 162–169) promotes "lens file missing or empty" from warning to **hard error → exit 1**.

Reproduced against a product-repo layout (`agents/` → this pack + a `.dmtools/config.js` carrying `reviewPolicy.required`):

```
✅ reviewer "base" (factory) — lens instructions/pr_review/generalist/lens.md | required:true | ...
❌ base: lens file missing or empty: instructions/pr_review/generalist/lens.md
❌ security: lens file missing or empty: instructions/pr_review/security/lens.md
reviewer pool: 2 reviewer(s) validated · 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)
❌ validate-review-skills: FAILED        # exit 1 — lenses exist; unfixable via --factory/--repo flags
```

Suggested fix: resolve factory-owned paths (lens, and any skill file path) against the discovered `packRoot` (fall back repoRoot-relative for repo-authored `.dmtools/review` paths — those are genuinely repo-root-relative, e.g. the valid fixture's `.dmtools/review/legal.lens.md`). A repo-vs-pack discriminator at the `io` bag keeps the pure `resolvePool` contract unchanged and lets a downstream repo actually use its §8 gate.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDORYAuYs629V2f` — **unknown** (`js/unit-tests/test_instructionRefs.js:246`)

🚨 severity: BLOCKING —
🚨 **BLOCKING: the rework that CRAP-split `walk` broke `v1ShimIndex` — R13's moved-target guard is now dead code (always green, never fires)**

The CRAP-split hunk (this rework) flipped the branch order inside `walk` (test_instructionRefs.js:243-250). The descent branch now runs **first for every entry**, but `file_exists` is an existence check for ANY path — boolean `true` in the dmtools host, `{exists: true}` in the node coverage harness (node_testRunner.js:328, predicate `function() { return true; }`). So every existing `.md` file enters `walk(rel)`; `file_list` on a file returns `null` → zero entries → the `else if (/\.md$/…)` shim-read branch at line 248 is unreachable for every real file. The index is always `{}`.

Evidence — the harness's exact host shapes against the real tree (file_exists on the shim → exists:true; file_list on it → null):

```
shim index size=0
file_exists(shim .md file) = {"exists":true}
file_list(that file) = null
```

Consequence: `R13 — "runner pack: refs … never pin a moved target while its v1 shim window is open" — can never fire` (test_instructionRefs.js:544-589). `shims` is `{}`, so `var shim = shims[p]; if (shim) …` never triggers, and the check silently degrades to the dangling-pin lookup only. The suite still passes — I re-ran it under the node harness (20 passed, 0 failed) — which is exactly why CI cannot see this. The guard demonstrably worked at `980ac31a` (it failed on the pre-980ac31a tree with the exact violation, per the discussion); the rework disconnected the sensor while keeping the light green.

This guard is the regression protection for the live `AgentPackException` crash class this PR itself hit (runner pins vs pack contents) — merging with it dead re-exposes the PR's documented follow-up (the planned flip of `.dmtools/runners/fa-review.json` to the v2 path) to the exact failure R13 exists to catch.

Fix (two parts):
1. Restore the read-before-descend order inside the split structure — `.md` files are files, never descent targets:
```javascript
if (/\.md$/.test(rel)) {
    shimBannerPaths(readText(rel)).forEach(function (live) { index[live] = rel; });
} else if (isTrueishExists(file_exists({ path: fsPath(rel) }))) {
    walk(rel);
}
```
2. Pin the composite so this can't regress silently: one end-to-end test asserting `v1ShimIndex()` contains the 7 shim paths (e.g. `index['instructions/pr_review/review_verdict_rules.md'] === 'instructions/pr_review/review_verdict_rules.md'`). The new characterization suite pins the four helpers but nothing pins the assembled index — that is the gap that let a green suite ship a dead guard.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:dmtools-factory-bot[bot]:2026-11-13:e2f86a78` — **dmtools-factory-bot[bot]** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-11-13

5. **Dig idioms.** Markers are the TOC. `session_search` locates, `compact_expand` reads. `read $FAH_SESSION_FILE:<line>` is the zero-tool fallback.

## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
2.5. **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: if the task ships a runnable verifier, test, or entry point the grader will call, run THAT command the way the grader will — neutral cwd (`cd /` — a different working directory, never the session cwd), fresh subprocess, clean env (no session-exported vars) — and compare stdout, stderr, and exit code against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` item to fix before finalizing. 2.6. **Conformance coverage** — applies ONLY when the final claim includes behavioral conformance: "matches the reference/specification", parity with an existing implementation, protocol/format compliance — any domain. Happy-path agreement certifies nothing about rejection paths or option combinations: two implementations agreeing on every well-formed input can still diverge exactly where one of them must say no. A conformance item counts as verified only when the checklist also quotes **negative and combination checks**, each one actually run and quoted in its ledger row: inputs that must be rejected or must error, combinations of incompatible/mutually exclusive options that must be refused, empty and corrupt inputs, boundary values, "must NOT work" / "must not find" cases — alongside the happy paths.
